info.bio: Charles Brown, nacido en Texas en 1922, se licencio en químicas y trató de abrirse camino como investigador, pero la guerra y la depresión económica, le llevó por el camino de la música y obtuvo en el piano el instrumento adecuado para ese fin. Comenzó su carrera en Los Ángeles. Actuó en el  Lincoln Theatre y en el  Chicken Shack de  Ivie Anderson antes de crear con el contrabajista  Eddie  Williams y el guitarrista  Johnny Moore, el trío  "The Three Blazers".

scenes.name: Rock'n'roll
scenes.author: Piero Scaruffi
scenes.desc: Fusión de rhythm'n'blues y country, con mucho más peso del primero. Chuck Berry inventa en 1955 el rock'n'roll tal como se conocerá durante cincuenta años (la guitarra como instrumento protagonista, canciones propias que hablan a los adolescentes); Bo Diddley aporta el ritmo «hambone», Little Richard y Esquerita el histerismo y el maquillaje (el primer «decadence-rock»), Jerry Lee Lewis el piano feroz y Sun Records el rockabilly. Elvis Presley es, para Scaruffi, «la primera gran estafa del rock'n'roll». Buddy Holly y Eddie Cochran abren otra vía; en paralelo nacen el soul (Ray Charles), la exótica (Martin Denny, Esquivel), la música electrónica de cinta y, en Gran Bretaña, el skiffle.

podcast.title: Blues Club Patronage
podcast.body: As a child, Jerry Lee Lewis would regularly sneak into a local blues club with an entirely Black clientele to watch performers like Charles Brown, Fats Domino, BB King, and Big Joe Turner until he was kicked out by the owner in the segregated South. "he would regularly sneak into a local blues club with an otherwise entirely black-cli-on-tail and hide under the table to watch people like Fat Stummino, Charles Brown, BB King, and Big Joe Turner."

podcast.title: Late Career Recordings
podcast.body: Charles Brown was among the artists whose late-career recordings were released by Johnny Otis's Blues Spectrum Records in the 1970s. Some of these recordings were Brown's last ever. "He ran blues spectrum records in the 70s, which put out late career recordings by people like Charles Brown, Big Joe Turner and Louis Jordan. Some of them their last ever recordings"

podcast.title: Major Early Influence on Ray Charles
podcast.body: Charles Brown, the singer for Johnny Moore's Three Blazers, was identified as another significant early influence on Ray Charles, whose trio initially adopted a similar smooth blues style. "Charles Brown, their singer, would be another huge influence on Ray Charles early arm."
